name: FBI 2026 identity-in-depth and facilitator-expansion guidance

attribution.legal_posture: The FBI publicly describes observed North Korean IT-worker tactics and defensive guidance in an October 2026 PSA; person-specific legal status requires a separate case source.

caveats: The PSA is generalized agency reporting; subject-level identity, facilitation, victim, account, and current-location status require separate sources.
identity_boundary: A technique and mitigation record drawn from the FBI PSA; its generalized observations need a separate source before attachment to a named person.

sources.support: The FBI PSA describes facilitator expansion, identity-in-depth detection, remote-access tooling, and escalation tactics.
sources.locator: Opening; Tips to Protect Your Business — Identity in Depth; Evolution of North Korean IT Worker Tactics

value.approach: multiple layered access controls and detections throughout the employment lifecycle

sources.locator: Tips to Protect Your Business — Identity in Depth, opening paragraphs
sources.quote: U.S. companies should recognize the scale, persistence, and rapid evolution of the North Korean ITW threat means ITWs cannot be identified reliably with a single indicator.

sources.locator: Tips to Protect Your Business — Identity in Depth, Identity in Depth paragraph
sources.quote: "Identity in Depth" — layered detections, access controls, and continuous identity verification throughout employment — avoids unreliable filters while enabling moderate, weak, or unavoidable signals to justify enhanced scrutiny when aggregated together.

notes: Defensive guidance; not a rule to reject applicants based on a single name or indicator.

services: keeping employment devices connected from residences

sources.locator: The general public needs to be aware paragraph
sources.quote: ITWs are paying Americans for an expanding range of services to hide their own involvement in the scheme, including asking some to appear on camera, participate in job interviews or meetings, verify fraudulent identities, provide access to personal social media or professional networking accounts, ship packages, complete urinalysis tests or fingerprint submissions, or keep employment-related devices connected to the Internet from personal residences.

notes: The PSA describes service categories only; no private account or identity data is retained.

sources.locator: Identity in Depth, behavioral tendencies and recommendations
sources.quote: ITWs continue to use remote desktop software to connect to employment-related devices. Examples include AnyDesk, TeamViewer, RustDesk, Chrome Remote Desktop, Splashtop Streamer, and remote monitoring and management (RMM) software.

sources.locator: Identity in Depth, behavioral tendencies and recommendations
sources.quote: ITWs use external hardware such as TinyPilot, PiKVM, GL.iNet, and other Keyboard Video Mouse (KVM) over IP devices to control laptops.

notes: Tool names are retained as defensive indicators; they are legitimate products and are not characterized as malicious by this record.

observations: threats of physical violence to demand payments

sources.quote: The FBI has observed North Korean ITWs use stolen identities, extort victims, and use threats of physical violence to demand payments.

notes: General FBI threat reporting; no victim or threat target is identified.
